correctness.rationale: Positive real overlap makes t=conj(w1)*w2 real; the two inverse-overlap branches for fixed nonzero w2 have a common phase. The ratio (1-t)/(1-beta*t) decreases strictly for beta<1, so the smaller t branch is forced for a maximum unless the branches agree at q=1. The radial transform has positive denominator and derivative with sign P. P decreases strictly from 1 to -2(1-beta)(1-h), because the bracket in P' is bounded above by -3(1-beta)(1-h). Its unique root gives all norming ordered pairs. Intermediate radii along the same branch and rotation attain the entire closed disk. At beta=1 the transform is q*w2 and attains only the open disk. The identity (1-r_*^2)^2=(1-beta)*r_*^2*(1-2*h*r_*+r_*^2) gives the boundary layer and its radius coefficient. For the other limit, the denominator is (1-r)(1+beta*r)+(1-beta)(1-h)r; this gives the upper bound and the matching test r=1-sqrt(q). The explicit pair at q=beta=1/2 has transform modulus 55/[6(47-15*sqrt(3))] > sqrt(3)/4, since 490^2>3*282^2.
residual_risks: Endpoint asymptotics fix the secondary parameter; no joint uniform limit is asserted.
